Recently, Indonesia signed a zero-tariff trade deal with the European Union. Around 20% of bilateral trade between these two regions falls under agriculture and food supply. It is another example of the increasing importance governments around the world are placing on food supply and agriculture.

Whether it is fertilizer, food, or agricultural machinery, there is no shortage of agriculture stocks looking to take advantage of this global focus.

Our Financially Healthy Agriculture Companies with High Insider Ownership screener aims to help investors find these stocks, looking for exciting small-cap agriculture stocks from around the world that have both healthy balance sheets and high insider ownership.

Below are three agriculture companies that insiders are backing.

Buffalo Potash (TSXV:BUFF)

Overview: Buffalo Potash is a Canadian explorer working to develop the Disley potash project in Saskatchewan, targeting fertilizer-grade potassium for long-term food security.

Market Cap: CA$95.5 million

With potash heavily concentrated, supply has become a critical focus for many countries looking to ensure food security. Buffalo’s Disley Project, along with its experimental technology, could help close the gap of what some are predicting is likely to be a potash deficit in the future.

The most-followed narrative on the Simply Wall St community highlights Buffalo’s progress towards making that opportunity a reality.

Its Disley Project has secured its final key regulatory approval, while a proposed C$8.5 million royalty deal with Altius Minerals provides funding without issuing new shares. First production is targeted for early 2027, although the company still needs to prove its technology at commercial scale.

According to Cezar, the community author, Buffalo potentially turning from mine development to production is a major stepping stone in the investment thesis:

“For a company this size, reaching real sales within about a year is the catalyst that changes everything.”

When a single variable can sway the whole build, the full narrative for Buffalo Potash explains how Buffalo Potash’s plan could accelerate or stall under different scenarios.

Sea Forest (ASX:SEA)

Overview: Sea Forest manufactures nature-identical bioactive feed additives in Australia, with its SeaFeed products directly targeting methane reduction and feed efficiency in livestock.

Operations: The business currently generates about A$5 million in food processing revenue, all from customers based in Australia.

Market Cap: A$79.3 million

Sea Forest matters for this screener because SeaFeed links climate-focused feed additives to food system productivity. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St outlines how policy, contracts, and carbon projects could mesh together for that agriculture story.

"Growing policy support for methane-reducing feed additives in Australia, including work on a dedicated ACCU method across beef, dairy, and sheep, could improve producer economics for adopting Sea Forest’s SeaFeed and support higher revenue and margins."

The key uncertainty is how quickly those early commercial wins convert into scaled, repeat orders, while managing production costs so they do not heavily reduce future margins.

Momentum on that front is exactly what the full narrative for Sea Forest unpacks, explaining how Sea Forest could turn policy tailwinds into accelerating, repeatable revenue.

Omer-Decugis & Cie (ENXTPA:ALODC)

Overview: Omer-Decugis & Cie supplies a wide range of fresh fruits and vegetables to French and international customers, directly serving everyday food demand.

Operations: The group generates about €244.6 million from its SIIM unit and €64.2 million from Bratigny, focused on fruit and vegetable distribution.

Market Cap: €50.3 million

Omer-Decugis & Cie is closely aligned with the screener theme through its core fresh produce distribution, with a P/E of 9.8x and forecast earnings growth of about 16.93% a year tied to bananas, mangoes and tomatoes that underpin basic food supply. Investors get direct exposure to food security, but the key consideration is how a thin 1.7% margin might behave if a single funding assumption shifts.

data.title: Is Eli Lilly (LLY) Undervalued As New FDA Eye Risk Warnings Hit GLP 1 Drugs?
data.description:

The label change landed in a market that has already priced in a lot of optimism around Eli Lilly, with the share price at US$1,392.22 and a 30-day share price return of 8.07% on top of a 90-day gain of 18.53% as investors digested strong GLP-1 driven results and recent oncology and obesity data. The 1-year total shareholder return of 30.24% and very large 5-year total shareholder return of 492.03% point to momentum that has been building over several years rather than a short-term spike.

According to AHaron, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who built the narrative, that spread rests on specific growth and earnings assumptions rather than vague optimism.

And earnings by 2031 of approximately $48 to $50 billion, above the model's $41.5 billion, because at 18% growth and stable margins, that is where the numbers actually land.

data.title: How Investors Are Reacting To Moderna (MRNA) Cancer Vaccine Progress
data.description:
• In November 2026, Moderna amended its credit agreement, cutting interest rate margins on its term loans, extending loan maturities to 2031, and lengthening the draw period on up to US$900 million of delayed draw commitments, while keeping guarantees and collateral terms in place.
  • Alongside this cheaper, longer-dated debt, Moderna has raised revenue guidance, improved its cash outlook, and reported positive Phase III data for an individualized cancer vaccine. Taken together, these developments clarify how the balance sheet could support oncology-focused investment.
  • This analysis will examine how Moderna's investment narrative is being reshaped by stronger cash outlook guidance that is anchored by positive individualized cancer vaccine trial results.

Moderna Investment Narrative Recap

To own Moderna, investors need to believe the mRNA platform can translate positive late stage data in vaccines and oncology into durable product demand and, in time, profits. That story now leans heavily on the individualized cancer vaccine and the broader respiratory vaccine suite, which together anchor management’s updated revenue and cash outlook.

The key near term catalyst is progress from the oncology franchise, especially regulatory milestones after the positive Phase III melanoma data. The biggest operational risk is execution across multiple launches while the business is still unprofitable and the share price remains volatile. The cheaper, longer dated debt does not materially change those core drivers.

According to LunaRodas, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the central question in the Moderna story is whether oncology and respiratory vaccines can justify the current valuation despite losses and a high P/S multiple. The amended credit agreement fits into that view by giving the group more room to fund that effort with lower interest costs and longer maturities.

The amendment trims rate margins by 0.75 percentage points and extends term loan maturities to 2031 while keeping up to US$900 million of delayed draw capacity in place. That may be important if oncology manufacturing and launch costs rise faster than anticipated, since management now has more flexibility to fund those programs without immediately relying on equity markets or near term cash flows.

LunaRodas anchors a fair value of US$230.15 per Moderna share mainly on the idea that the first positive Phase III result for an individualized cancer vaccine, combined with explicit oncology funding through the US$3b convertible, supports a materially richer mRNA oncology platform story.

Exploring Other Perspectives

For Moderna, the bullish twist in the alternate narrative is that some analysts were already banking on oncology and rare disease programs as major earnings engines. Before this debt amendment, the most optimistic forecasts were for revenue to reach about US$8.0b and earnings of US$1.6b by 2029, with a US$305 price target. That is a far more ambitious story than the baseline, and none of those forecasts yet reflect cheaper, longer term borrowing.
